source.title: Data Centre Backup Power Supply Market to Reach USD 17.15 Billion by 2034 as AI and Hyperscale Infrastructure Expand
source.body:
Global Data Centre Backup Power Supply Market was valued at USD 8.21 billion in 2025 and is estimated to reach USD 8.90 billion in 2026. According to EnergyResourcesInsights, the market is projected to reach USD 17.15 billion by 2034, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8.5% during 2026–2034. Increasing investments in hyperscale data Centres, artificial intelligence infrastructure, cloud computing and high-performance computing are strengthening demand for reliable backup power equipment and integrated energy storage solutions.

[https://www.EnergyResourcesInsights.com/data-Centre-backup-power-supply-market-1313](https://www.energyresourcesinsights.com/data-center-backup-power-supply-market-1313)

Data Centre backup power supplies maintain electricity availability for critical computing, storage, networking and cooling equipment during utility interruptions and planned switching events. The market includes uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, integrated energy storage, standby generators, battery energy storage systems and fuel cells. Growing computing workloads and increasingly stringent uptime requirements are encouraging operators to invest in advanced backup power architectures.

Market at a Glance

·         2025 market size: USD 8.21 billion

·         2026 estimate: USD 8.90 billion

·         2034 forecast: USD 17.15 billion

·         Forecast CAGR: 8.5% during 2026–2034

·         Leading region: North America, with an estimated 45% of 2025 revenue

·         Leading product segment: UPS Systems & Integrated Energy Storage, accounting for approximately 46% of 2025 revenue

·         Leading application: Hyperscale AI Training & Inference Facilities, representing approximately 55% of 2025 revenue

AI Infrastructure and Data Centre Expansion Drive Demand

The growing deployment of cloud computing, generative AI and high-performance computing is increasing the need for dependable electrical infrastructure. Data Centres require continuous electricity to maintain server operations, cooling systems and network availability. Even short interruptions can affect computing workloads, operational continuity and service reliability.

Backup power infrastructure typically combines UPS systems, batteries and generator sets to provide protection across different interruption durations. UPS systems and batteries respond immediately to electrical disturbances, while standby generators provide longer-duration backup during extended utility outages.

Artificial intelligence workloads are also changing equipment requirements. GPU clusters can produce rapid and synchronized power fluctuations, requiring advanced power electronics and generator systems capable of responding to dynamic electrical loads. Suppliers are therefore developing higher-capacity UPS platforms, modular backup systems and integrated energy management solutions.

Grid capacity constraints are creating another important market opportunity. Data Centre developers increasingly evaluate battery energy storage, on-site generation and microgrid controls as part of their infrastructure planning. These solutions can support commissioning, improve operational flexibility and strengthen resilience where utility connections face delays.

Key Market Drivers and Challenges

Several factors are shaping the industry's outlook:

·         Hyperscale data Centre expansion: New cloud and AI facilities require substantial backup power capacity to protect critical workloads.

·         Increasing electricity consumption: Growing computing requirements are increasing the need for reliable power infrastructure.

·         AI and HPC deployment: High-density accelerator workloads require advanced UPS and backup systems capable of handling rapid load changes.

·         Grid infrastructure constraints: Limited utility capacity and connection delays are encouraging interest in integrated storage and on-site generation.

·         Reliability requirements: Data Centre operators prioritize redundancy, power continuity, equipment monitoring and operational resilience.

The market also faces challenges. High capital expenditure, generator emissions regulations, battery replacement costs and complex electrical integration can affect purchasing decisions. Equipment qualification, maintenance availability, fuel logistics and the coordination of multiple power sources remain important considerations for operators.

Segmentation and Regional Outlook

The market is segmented by product type, application, power architecture and end user.

·         Type: UPS Systems & Integrated Energy Storage, Standby Generators & Gensets, Battery Energy Storage Systems, and Fuel Cells & Alternative Backup Systems.

·         Application: Hyperscale AI Training & Inference Facilities, Colocation AI Campuses, Enterprise & Sovereign AI Data Centres, and Edge AI & Distributed Compute.

·         Power architecture: Online Double-Conversion UPS with Lithium-Ion Storage, Dynamic UPS/Rotary UPS, Generator-Backed AC Architectures, and 800 VDC & Integrated Multi-Timescale Storage.

·         End user: Hyperscale Cloud & AI Platform Operators, Colocation & Wholesale Data Centre Operators, Enterprise & Sovereign AI Operators, and Managed Service & Edge Infrastructure Providers.

North America led the market with an estimated 45% share of 2025 revenue. The region benefits from substantial hyperscale investment, established cloud infrastructure and expanding AI computing capacity. Asia-Pacific accounted for approximately 25% of 2025 revenue, supported by data Centre construction across China, Japan, Singapore, Australia and Southeast Asia.

Europe remains an important market due to cloud infrastructure development and demand for reliable electricity systems. Latin America and the Middle East & Africa offer additional opportunities through expanding digital infrastructure and new data Centre investments.

Competitive Landscape

The competitive environment spans power electronics, energy storage, generator systems, switchgear and critical-power controls. Key companies covered in the report include Vertiv, Schneider Electric, Eaton, Caterpillar, Cummins, ABB, Delta Electronics, Huawei Digital Power, Rehlko, Rolls-Royce Power Systems, Mitsubishi Electric and Socomec.

Companies are competing through integrated power solutions, higher-capacity UPS systems, generator efficiency, battery integration, equipment reliability and global service capabilities. The ability to coordinate multiple backup technologies within a unified power architecture is becoming increasingly important.
